# goal/riders/: amendment riders for reusable `/goal` templates

A rider is a small git-tracked markdown file that amends one armed goal. A reusable template's text
is fixed and digest-checked, so anything one arming needs beyond it goes in a rider. The usual case
is a list of in-progress tasks the goal should leave out. A rider can also add an S-item or an exit
term. The design is the "Goal amendment riders" design doc under ai-harness's `docs/designs/`.

Status: this directory's contract is in force. `/start-goal --amendment <path>`, `start_goal.py
rider new` and `start_goal.py rider check` consume it.

## Which copy to read

The ai-harness copies of this README, [`TEMPLATE.md`](TEMPLATE.md) and [`STUB.md`](STUB.md) are
canonical. A consumer repo carries this README as a pointer copy and resolves STUB and TEMPLATE in
this order:

1. its own `docs/prompts/goal/riders/STUB.md` or `TEMPLATE.md`, kept only when the repo has a
   use-case-specific shape;
2. otherwise the ai-harness copy, `~/projects/ai-harness/docs/prompts/goal/riders/`.

A repo with no use-case-specific need keeps neither file.

## Where riders live and how they are named

- Path: `<repo>/docs/prompts/goal/riders/<YYMMDD>-<slug>.md`. The repo is any repo under the
  projects root and defaults to ai-harness. Put the rider in the repo whose tasks it amends.
- Name: the date the rider was written (UTC), then a short lowercase hyphenated slug.
- Reference: the path relative to the projects root, for example
  `ai-harness/docs/prompts/goal/riders/261018-skip-two.md`. It is at most 80 characters, because
  the goal condition carries it.
- A rider in a public repo (`public_repos` in ai-harness's `config/start-goal.toml`) names no
  private task id. Elsewhere it may.

## What a rider contains

Start from the rider STUB and follow the rider TEMPLATE, both resolved as in
[Which copy to read](#which-copy-to-read). The frontmatter
records the invocation: when the rider was written (`created_at`, UTC with a `Z`), who wrote it
(`created_by`, `<session>@<AI_HOST>`), which templates it may arm (`amends`), the Beads issue it
serves (`issue`), where the instruction came from (`ask`), the rider it replaces (`supersedes`) and
an optional list of Beads ids left out of scope (`exclude`).

The body has two sections. `## Amendment` binds the goal, one numbered sentence per change: a
scope change, or an added S-item with its own `verify:` and `evidence:`, or an added exit term.
`## Why` quotes the instruction behind it, verbatim.

A rider can only narrow or add. It never grants an authority the goal or the context files
withhold, so a rider that says "you may push to a shared repo" is invalid.

## Binding, reuse and change

- Land the rider on its repo's default branch before arming it, through the repo's normal PR
  route. Arming binds that exact file version by its git blob id.
- A merged rider is never edited. A second commit to it is refused, both at commit time and at
  arming.
- Reuse means arming the same path again; the bound text is identical.
- Any change means a new rider: copy the old one, edit it, and set `supersedes` to the old path.

## How the evaluator sees it

The native `/goal` evaluator reads only the condition and the conversation, never a file. Arming
puts one short clause naming the rider's path and blob id in the condition. A hook injects the
rider's full bound text into the conversation at arming and at the start of every window,
compaction and resume included. The clause says an unseen rider means not met. So if the text is
missing, the evaluator rejects and names the rider, and the session repairs that by reading the
file.

Read the rider in full on every check, as the session and as the evaluator. Its Amendment counts
toward SUCCESS and TERMINATION exactly like the template's own text.
